foodAndKitchen.standfirst: More wheat bought for the public stores, and onions and food prices on the rise.

workAndWages.title: Work and wages
workAndWages.standfirst: A new rural jobs law, a social security fund for delivery riders, and the khadi workforce.

items.title: A new rural jobs law
items.summary: The VB-G RAM G law took effect on 1 July 2026, replacing the MGNREGA rural employment guarantee, and the first Rs 25,863 crore was released to states on 5 July.

sources.label: Wikipedia: 2026 in India

items.title: A fund for platform workers
items.summary: Under the labour codes notified in November 2025, delivery and ride apps must pay 1 to 2 percent of their annual turnover, within caps, into a social security fund for gig workers.

spotlight.title: Ten-minute deliveries and the gig worker

items.title: The Labour Ministry steps in
items.summary: In mid-January 2026 the Labour Ministry asked quick-commerce platforms to stop advertising 10-minute delivery guarantees, after a meeting about road safety, work pressure and gig workers' conditions.

items.title: The tagline changes
items.summary: Blinkit replaced '10,000+ products delivered in 10 minutes' with '30,000+ products delivered at your doorstep'; Eternal said the change would not materially affect its business.

sources.label: Storyboard18: Qcomm branding reset, Blinkit, Instamart, Zepto and the retreat from 10-minute delivery (14 January 2026)

items.title: A strike on New Year's Eve
items.summary: Delivery workers struck nationwide on New Year's Eve over pay, insurance and ultra-fast targets; on 5 January a delivery worker was killed in an accident in Hyderabad, and a union raised concerns about delivery timelines.

sources.label: The Week: Blinkit stops '10 minute' delivery claim; Zepto follows suit (13 January 2026)

items.title: The company's side
items.summary: Blinkit's chief executive said that in 2025 the average order travelled 2.03 km, with about 8 minutes of driving, an average speed of roughly 16 km/h, and that delivery partners were not overworked.

items.summary: India's quick-commerce companies were reported in January 2026 to be nearing Rs 10,000 crore in quarterly revenue, with most deliveries taking 10 to 20 minutes.
